extracted.intended_audience: general public and researchers interested in CRI funding (potential applicants, donors, and cancer immunology community)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Cancer Research Institute's funding priorities, eligible recipients, award programs, and activities supporting cancer immunotherapy research. Useful for understanding who and what CRI funds and how it engages the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on immunological treatments for cancer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute focuses on immunological treatments for cancer, both single treatment approaches and treatments complementing chemotherapy and surgery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRI prioritizes research and interventions centered on immuno-oncology; funding and activities are oriented toward projects that advance immunological approaches, including combination strategies with existing modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients for research grants
rubrics_metrics.description: It offers research grants to students, postdoctoral fellows, and investigators at medical research institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRI funds a range of career stages with explicit support for students and postdoctoral fellows and also funds investigators at institutional research centers; historically emphasizes early-career researcher support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding of clinical trials testing promising immunotherapies
rubrics_metrics.description: It funds clinical trials testing promising immunotherapies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRI provides support that extends beyond basic research to clinical translation, backing trials that test immunotherapy candidates deemed promising by the Institute and its advisory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convenes scientific conferences for tumor immunologists
rubrics_metrics.description: It convenes scientific conferences for tumor immunologists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRI organizes meetings (including an annual symposium) to bring together researchers in immuno-oncology, which also serve as venues for announcements and community-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors annual awards and postdoctoral fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute sponsors a number of annual awards in the field of cancer research, and dozens of postdoctoral fellowships. Awards are announced at the Institute's annual symposium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named awards (e.g., William B. Coley Award, Lloyd J. Old Award, Frederick W. Alt Award, Oliver R. Grace Award, Helen Coley Nauts Award) recognize scientists whose research has had a major impact on immunology; CRI also supports numerous postdoctoral fellowships—award decisions are tied to the Institute's annual events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance and scientific advisory oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Its work is guided by a scientific advisory council that includes four Nobel laureates and 35 members of the National Academy of Sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRI employs a high-level advisory structure implying peer review and rigorous scientific vetting of priorities and funded work; prospective applicants can expect programmatic decisions informed by eminent scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and support of community resources and collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2020, CRI collaborated with Sage Bionetworks to produce an interactive online atlas of research datasets in immuno-oncology (CRI iAtlas). In 2025, it funded a Mount Sinai immunotherapy lab to study outcomes across CRI's clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRI supports infrastructure and partner collaborations (data portals, institutional labs) that enable broader research efforts and trial outcome studies, indicating funding can include resource-building and collaborative projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and historical funding impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1953, CRI has distributed over $500 million in grants, supporting over 3000 scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization's long history and funding scale demonstrate significant capacity and sustained commitment to the field; this contextualizes competitiveness and reach of CRI-funded programs.
